newsitem.title: USA: FCC - schools, libraries may contract for discounted services. [CORRECTED 10:00 GMT 12/7]
newsitem.headline: FCC - schools, libraries may contract for discounted services. [CORRECTED 10:00 GMT 12/7]

text.p: The Federal Communications Commission on Thursday extended an exemption for schools or libraries contracting out telecommunications services to comply with a competitive bidding mandate created in the Telecommunications Act of 1996.
This will permit schools and libraries to sign contracts before the competitive bidding requirement is in place and still receive universal service discounts.
(Corrects to clarify FCC has extended an exemption not suspended a requirement. Clarifies exemption terms).

On its own motion, the FCC concluded that any school or library eligible for universal service discounts is not required to comply with the competitive bidding requirement for any contract for telecommunications services that it signs after November 8, 1996 and before the competitive bidding system is operational.
This is limited to services provided to the institution before December 31, 1998.
In addition, the Commission clarified that an eligible establishment may not receive a federal universal service discount on services provided to it before January 1, 1998.
